title: 94. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Comparing Ratios with Common Units
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios in the Same Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two ratios with the same units and identify the greater ratio.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(3:4\) or \(2:3\)?
questions.explanation: Compare the ratios by writing them as fractions: \(\frac{3}{4}=0.75\) and \(\frac{2}{3}\approx0.667\). Since \(0.75>0.667\), the ratio \(3:4\) is greater. The other ratio has the smaller quotient.
questions.hint: Write each ratio as a fraction and compare the resulting values.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios After Converting to Common Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two length ratios by converting both to the same unit.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(1.5\text{ m}:2\text{ m}\) or \(150\text{ cm}:250\text{ cm}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert the first ratio to centimetres: \(1.5\text{ m}=150\text{ cm}\) and \(2\text{ m}=200\text{ cm}\), so the ratio is \(150:200=3:4=0.75\). The second ratio is \(150:250=3:5=0.6\). Since \(0.75>0.6\), the first ratio is greater. The other ratio has the smaller quotient after unit conversion.
questions.hint: Convert both quantities in each ratio to the same unit before comparing.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Units in Context
questions.learningObjective: Compare two distance-to-time ratios by converting to a common unit rate.
questions.question: Compare \(60\text{ km}:2\text{ h}\) and \(90\text{ km}:3\text{ h}\). Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Find the unit rate for each ratio. \(60\text{ km}:2\text{ h}\) gives \(60\div2=30\text{ km/h}\). \(90\text{ km}:3\text{ h}\) gives \(90\div3=30\text{ km/h}\). Since both ratios represent \(30\text{ km/h}\), they are equal. The alternative looks only at the shorter time in the first ratio (\(2\text{ h}<3\text{ h}\)) and ignores that the distance is proportionally shorter as well.
questions.hint: Write each ratio as a quotient with the same unit in the denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Compare two mass ratios after converting grams and kilograms to the same unit.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(500\text{ g}:2\text{ kg}\) or \(1\text{ kg}:3\text{ kg}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert the first ratio to grams: \(2\text{ kg}=2000\text{ g}\), so \(500:2000=1:4=0.25\). The second ratio is \(1:3\approx0.333\). Since \(0.333>0.25\), the second ratio is greater. The other ratio has the smaller quotient after converting to common units.
questions.hint: Convert kilograms to grams before writing each ratio as a fraction.

questions.learningObjective: Compare two ratios using cross multiplication.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(3:7\) or \(2:5\)?
questions.explanation: Compare \(\frac{3}{7}\) and \(\frac{2}{5}\) by cross multiplication: \(3\times5=15\) and \(2\times7=14\). Since \(15>14\), the fraction \(\frac{3}{7}\) is greater. Therefore, the ratio \(3:7\) is greater. The other ratio has the smaller cross product after using a common denominator.
questions.hint: Cross multiply the numerator of each fraction by the denominator of the other.

questions.learningObjective: Compare two time ratios after converting minutes and hours to the same unit.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(20\text{ min}:1\text{ h}\) or \(45\text{ min}:2\text{ h}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert hours to minutes. The first ratio is \(20:60=1:3\approx0.333\). The second ratio is \(45:120=3:8=0.375\). Since \(0.375>0.333\), the second ratio is greater. The other ratio has the smaller quotient after converting both times to minutes.
questions.hint: Convert every time to minutes, then compare the simplified ratios.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Mixed Length Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two length ratios by converting metres and centimetres to a common unit.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(0.5\text{ m}:50\text{ cm}\) or \(0.8\text{ m}:40\text{ cm}\)?
questions.explanation: Convert metres to centimetres. The first ratio is \(50:50=1:1=1\). The second ratio is \(80:40=2:1=2\). Since \(2>1\), the second ratio is greater. The other ratio has the smaller quotient after unit conversion.
questions.hint: Convert both lengths in each ratio to centimetres before comparing.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether two ratios are equal after simplifying.
questions.question: Compare \(12:18\) and \(10:15\). Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Simplify each ratio. \(12:18\) divides by \(6\) to give \(2:3\). \(10:15\) divides by \(5\) to give \(2:3\). Both simplify to \(2:3\), so the two ratios are equal. The alternative compares raw terms without accounting for equivalent scaling.
questions.hint: Simplify both ratios to lowest terms before comparing them.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios with Different Quantity Units
questions.learningObjective: Compare two ratios involving mass and volume by comparing their fractional values.
questions.question: Which ratio is greater, \(3\text{ kg}:5\text{ L}\) or \(4\text{ kg}:6\text{ L}\)?
questions.explanation: Write each ratio as a fraction. \(\frac{3}{5}=0.6\) and \(\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}\approx0.667\). Since \(0.667>0.6\), the ratio \(4\text{ kg}:6\text{ L}\) is greater. The other ratio has the smaller mass per litre.
questions.hint: Write each ratio as a fraction in lowest terms and compare the values.

questions.concept: Comparing Ratios in a Mixture Context
questions.learningObjective: Compare two concentrate-to-water ratios to determine which mixture is stronger.
questions.question: Mixture P uses concentrate and water in the ratio \(2:5\). Mixture Q uses concentrate and water in the ratio \(3:8\). Which mixture is stronger?
questions.explanation: A stronger mixture has a greater concentrate-to-water ratio. Compare \(\frac{2}{5}=0.4\) and \(\frac{3}{8}=0.375\). Since \(0.4>0.375\), Mixture P has the greater concentrate-to-water ratio and is stronger. The other mixture has the smaller concentrate-to-water ratio.
questions.hint: Compare the concentrate-to-water ratios by writing them as fractions.
